neighbours.label: gravity, weight and falling (weightlessness, free fall, things dropping or pulled down)
fire: In orbit, astronauts feel weightless because they are constantly falling toward Earth.
A dropped hammer and a feather fall at the same rate on the Moon.
The pull of gravity keeps the ball from flying off into space.
When the elevator cable snapped, the passengers floated toward the ceiling.
A skydiver speeds up until air resistance balances her weight.
On Jupiter you would weigh more than twice as much as on Earth.
The apple fell straight down from the branch onto the grass.
Engineers tested the parachute by dropping a heavy sandbag from the plane.
quiet: In a magnet, the north pole attracts the south pole of another magnet.
A hot cup of tea slowly loses heat to the cooler air around it.
Light bends when it passes from air into water.
Sound travels faster through steel than through air.
An electric current flows when the circuit is closed.
Friction between the tires and the road helps a car stop.
Ice melts into water when the temperature rises above zero.
Engineers tested the motor by running it at full speed for an hour.

notes: Card: top examples are weightlessness, falling floors, downward force, being pinned; - pole is body orientation / tucking.
